req.title: Redirect-to supports custom status codes
req.statement: The system shall honour the 'status_code' query parameter on /redirect-to for values 301, 302, 303, 307, and 308.

doc.reasoning: The redirect_to() handler reads 'status_code' from query args, validates it is in [300,400), and sets response.status_code accordingly. To kill mutations we must: (1) assert exact status codes for each valid value (301,302,303,307,308); (2) test the boundary at 300 (inclusive lower bound) and 399 (inclusive upper bound); (3) test 299 and 400 which must NOT change the default 302; (4) verify the Location header is set to the exact url supplied; (5) test missing status_code defaults to 302; (6) test non-redirect status_code values are ignored. This covers EP, BVA, DT, NEG heuristics and catches operator-flip mutations (>= vs >, < vs <=), constant mutations (302->303, 300->301, 400->399), and boolean/branch mutations.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_status_301
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_status_301():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=301', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 301
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_status_301()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact
actions: GET /redirect-to with each of 301,302,303,307,308 and assert exact status code returned
expected: Each status_code param value is reflected exactly in the response status code
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact():
    for code in [301, 302, 303, 307, 308]:
        r = client.get(
            '/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=' + str(code),
            follow_redirects=False
        )
        assert r.status_code == code, f'Expected {code}, got {r.status_code}'
        assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_boundary_301_vs_300_distinct
actions: GET /redirect-to with status_code=300 and then 301, assert each returns its own exact code
expected: 301 returns 301 — catches off-by-one mutation on lower bound
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_boundary_301_vs_300_distinct():
    r300 = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://a.com&status_code=300', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r300.status_code == 300
    r301 = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://a.com&status_code=301', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r301.status_code == 301
    assert r300.status_code != r301.status_code

test_redirect_to_boundary_301_vs_300_distinct()
